subject.title: Session files should never be deleted — rename .deleted.* to .archived.*

question: Should OpenClaw change the shipped session transcript archive contract from `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` plus retention cleanup to a durable `.archived.*` or `sessions/archive/` model, and should archive transcripts ever be physically removed automatically?
rationale: The current behavior is implemented across storage, maintenance, archive helpers, docs, and disk-budget cleanup; changing it affects existing on-disk data and operator expectations, so maintainer intent is required before a repair PR.

options.title: Adopt durable archive semantics
options.body: Rename or relocate retained transcripts, add migration/doctor coverage for existing archive files, and make physical deletion opt-in or separately configured.

options.title: Clarify current semantics only
options.body: Keep `.deleted.*`/`.reset.*` and retention cleanup but document that these are retained artifacts only until maintenance or disk budget removes them.

options.title: Fix only concrete hard-delete paths
options.body: Leave the naming policy unchanged and continue repairing narrow defects like the already-merged role-ordering reset unlink path.

recommendation.title: Adopt durable archive semantics
recommendation.body: Rename or relocate retained transcripts, add migration/doctor coverage for existing archive files, and make physical deletion opt-in or separately configured.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest available history signal for the broader session archive filesystem/runtime path is prior source-seam/refactor work by Peter Steinberger.
